takeaways: There is a way to skip blocks of content that repeat on many pages, such as the header, navigation and side menus.
Without it, keyboard and switch users press Tab through every navigation link on every page before reaching the content.
Common ways to meet it are a “Skip to main content” link, headings at the start of each section, and landmark regions such as header, nav and main.
Designers decide the skip link’s design and position, the heading structure and the regions of each template. Developers build them.
failures: Fifty navigation links before the main content, with no skip link
A skip link that is hidden even when it receives focus
A skip link that goes to the wrong place, or nowhere
check: In each page template, mark the blocks that repeat and the regions: header, navigation, main, footer.
Design the skip link’s focused state and check it appears first in the focus order.
In the build, press Tab once on a page and Enter on the skip link, then check that the next Tab lands inside the main content.

quiz.question: The team wants a skip link but feels it looks out of place in the header. What do you design?
options: Leave it out, because screen readers can use headings instead
Hide it until it receives keyboard focus, then show it clearly at the top left
Put it in the footer so it does not disturb the design
quiz.why: A skip link that appears on focus keeps the header clean and helps sighted keyboard users, who cannot jump by headings. In the footer, people would already have tabbed past everything.

spec: Design the skip link’s focused state: wording, position, size and contrast.
Mark the regions of each template, such as header, navigation, main and footer, and where the skip link goes.
If there are several repeated blocks, such as a long filter panel, note any extra skip links.
review: How many Tab presses does it take to reach the content?
Where does the skip link appear, and can sighted keyboard users see it?
Are the page regions marked in the file?
tradeoff: A visible skip link can feel like clutter. Showing it only on keyboard focus keeps the look clean, while still being there for the people who need it.
system: Build the skip link and page regions into the page layout template, so every new page has them by default.
pitch: Without a skip link, a keyboard user presses Tab through our whole menu on every single page. One link fixes that.
